title: Multi-Expert Seizure Annotation
description: Stereotactic EEG recordings of 78 seizures (44 spontaneous, 34 stimulation-induced) from 29 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, recruited at the University of Pennsylvania and the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. Three or five board-certified epileptologists independently annotated each seizure for onset time, onset channels, and channels seizing 10 seconds after onset, following a standardized protocol. The BIDS-formatted data include electrode localizations, patient demographics, and clinical outcomes. They serve as a benchmark for validating automated seizure onset and spread detection against expert consensus, and for comparing networks of spontaneous and stimulation-induced seizures.
methods_description: Stereotactic EEG was recorded with a Natus Quantum system at 512-2048 Hz using Ad-Tech (HUP) or PMT/DIXI (CHOP) depth electrodes. Recordings were referenced to a contact in presumed non-epileptogenic tissue, typically medullary bone. Stimulation-induced seizures used bipolar biphasic stimulation at 1-2 Hz, 1-8 mA, 300-500 µs pulse width. Electrodes were localized by co-registering post-implant CT to pre-implant MRI, with Desikan-Killiany parcellation in FreeSurfer. Multiple experts annotated seizure onset using a standardized protocol.
